title: Eshadhi Bogoda
text: I am currently a Master of Data Science (MDS) student at the University of British Columbia. Prior to joining the program, I worked as a Learning Systems Analyst at STEMCELL Technologies for nearly four years and I earned my Bachelor of Health Sciences from Simon Fraser University. Through the MDS program, I am developing technical data science skills to support a career transition into data focused roles. My goal is to apply data science and analytics to improve decision-making and outcomes in healthcare.

title: About
text:
I grew up in Metro Vancouver and studied at Simon Fraser University, where I earned a Bachelor of Health Sciences with a concentration in Population Health and a minor in Computer and Electronic Design. Before starting the Master of Data Science (MDS) program at UBC, I worked at STEMCELL Technologies as a Learning Systems Analyst. What I loved about my job was to help support learning in a professional setting even after leaving school.


My background in health sciences sparked my interest in the power of data and the insights it can provide. While I am particularly interested in applying data science to healthcare initiatives, planning and decision-making, I am also excited by its potential across a variety of industries. Through data science, I enjoy uncovering patterns, answering meaningful questions and discovering the stories that data can tell. I hope to use these skills to support data-driven solutions that create a positive impact.



Outside of data science, you can usually find me with a book. I enjoy reading, staying active and spending quality time with friends and family. I also love to bake and decorate cakes.

title: My First Weeks in MDS
text:
First Week in MDS
Orientation
Orientation for MDS was a whirlwind of emotions. Lots of excitements and eager to meet my new classmates but also anxious about what the next 10 months will be like. The first day was a lot of information to take in but on the next day the scavenger hunt was a great way to explore the campus and get to know some classmates.
First Week of Class
First weeks of classes was tougher than I thought it would be but I also learned how to use the terminal which was really fun. I also did not expect the assignments to take as long as they did. What surprised me the most was how quickly I got used to being a student working full time right up to the start of orientation.
Current Thoughts
In week 2, I mostly think about what the next week will be like and try to finish my assignments soon so I have enough time to study as well.
